data.description:
## Why
Spinner-only titles from agent TUIs are published as real title changes. Forty agents means a steady stream of metadata writes and sidebar wakes for a glyph that is not a name. Backlog item: B061.

## Evidence
origin/main `0ff8887e5e`, verified.

- `GHOSTTY_ACTION_SET_TITLE` in `Sources/GhosttyTerminalView.swift` (the case just above `GHOSTTY_ACTION_PWD`, about 2218) posts `.ghosttyDidSetTitle` for every string, including a spinner frame.
- `Sources/WorkspaceManager.swift:1065` coalesces those notifications at 30 Hz (`NotificationBurstCoalescer`, observer at `:1141`). The coalesce still applies each distinct string, including the metadata write and the window title. There is no spinner filter.
- Upstream cmux #10351 (`bd1288e5dc`) strips a standalone spinner glyph before publish (`TerminalTitleChurnFilter`).
- Research: Fable cluster C5, wave 1. Round 1 already deduped window titles. This is the missing filter.

## Scope
In: a title that is only a spinner glyph, or only a spinner plus the previous title, does not write `SurfaceMetadataStore` and does not set `window.title`. A real title change still does, including a title that contains a spinner plus words.

Out:
- Wakeup and scrollbar coalescing (B030). Same file, different case in the action switch. Do not change tick behavior.
- PWD routing through the key window (B137). That is the next case in the same switch. Leave it. It is on the tier-2 sweep.
- Portal views that subscribe to every title (B160). Tier-2 sweep. Filtering the producer is this ticket. Unsubscribing is not.
- Event-log title dedupe (C11-232). Neighbor. Do not take it over.
- Sidebar snapshot work (B059).

## Approach
A small pure filter: if the new title's meaningful text equals the last published title once spinner glyphs are removed, drop it. Publish the first real title and any later real change. Keep the 30 Hz coalescer. Do not slow it down to hide the spinner. The filter runs before the metadata write.

Use the glyph set upstream uses, adapted if c11's agents emit a different spinner. Name the glyphs in the PR. A title that is empty stays empty. Do not invent a fallback name.

## Acceptance criteria
1. A terminal whose program emits a spinner frame several times a second does not update the tab subtitle or the window title on those frames. A following real title, such as the command name, still appears.
2. Two different real titles in a row both appear. The filter does not freeze the first title forever.
3. The focused window's title still tracks the focused tab's real title.

## Validation
A pure test of the filter: spinner-only in, no change out. Real title in, change out. No `NSApp`. A tagged build glance is enough for the window title, on Atlas after C11-216. No soak. No source-grep test.

## Dependencies
None inside ws:bugs. Cross-workstream: F1 is C11-216 only for the glance. The lead links it.

## Risks
A filter that drops real titles which happen to use a braille or block glyph as content. Limit it to a standalone spinner, or spinner characters wrapping an unchanged title. Doctrine: no tenant config. No new strings. Public repo: a title filter, not a list of agent control sequences.

Size: S. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: drop spinner frames before the metadata write.

Validator scenario

1. Build merged main on Atlas with a unique tag; record its SHA and the pre-change comparison SHA 7bb785741750ddeb8ab12b4cf6472593fb8c3550. Launch with QA fresh. Use only the tagged app and a synthetic workspace, verify the target display, set a hard termination timer, and prove synthesized dismissal before concluding. Expected: production c11 and its workspaces remain untouched.
2. In one terminal, emit OSC 0 title claude (printf '\033]0;claude\007'). Capture its tab title/OSC metadata and window title. Emit standalone frames and frames surrounding claude several times per second for two seconds, covering Braille, U+2731–U+273D/✢/·, half-circles and quadrant circles. Expected: the title remains claude; frames produce no title metadata changes or visible tab animation. Capture screenshots and observer/metadata evidence where available. The window title retains the existing workspace-title policy.
3. Emit npm test, wait for the existing coalescer, then git status. Expected: each real title appears. In one write emit claude, npm test, claude ◐ before the coalescer flushes; then emit claude ◓. Expected: the final admitted raw title is claude ◐ and the subsequent frame is suppressed; a stale downstream baseline must not leave npm test displayed.
4. Emit an empty OSC title, followed by a standalone spinner, then a real title. Expected: OSC metadata clears without the filter inventing a fallback, the spinner does not replace the clear, and the following real title publishes. Record any existing UI fallback separately from OSC metadata.
5. Emit A·B then AB, block █ chart, an unrecognized Braille glyph ⠑, and a Braille word/art run such as ⠋ ⠑⠇⠇⠕. Expected: each meaningful change publishes; embedded glyphs and adjacent glyph runs survive. Repeat real titles in a second terminal. Expected: independent terminals retain independent OSC baselines and existing focus/window-title behavior.
6. Repeat the same short spinner/real-title sequence and a fixed small input interaction on a tagged Atlas build of the pre-change SHA with identical topology. Record both timings and load averages; compare observed title churn and input responsiveness. Expected: filtered frames stop causing title churn without a new input delay. This is the deferred-soak replacement, not a fleet soak. Save the fixture, metadata captures, screenshots and timing/load evidence; dismiss the tagged test windows with synthesized input.

Reviewed PR #513 at head 84acb43ce6d1d5f1589512b1ede45f1d0341dd0c against merge-base 7bb785741750ddeb8ab12b4cf6472593fb8c3550. Remote branch still matches the pinned head; origin/main was aa292e8f1c4ee95def5b3d9341a58d1a5553037c. Reviewed all four changed files, the task and current plan, validation event ev_01M3XMEW9FRC1QV9XMPXYEGRBD, repository policies, and the downstream notification/coalescer/metadata/title display paths.

## Blocking

None found.

## Non-blocking

None requiring changes.

The per-TerminalSurface filter advances its admitted OSC baseline before posting .ghosttyDidSetTitle. Spinner-only and unchanged-label frame notifications return before all three observers, eliminating their associated metadata/coalescer and titlebar/toolbar work. The existing 30 Hz coalescer and metadata precedence remain downstream; the rapid claude -> npm test -> claude-with-frame sequence does not compare against stale displayed metadata. Real changes retain their raw title, explicit clears remain distinct from spinner-only input, and the finite glyph set plus embedded/adjacent-glyph preservation implements the plan's false-positive boundary.

The added work is confined to the existing OSC-title main-queue hop: linear string scans/tokenization with temporary allocations, no I/O or new scheduling mechanism. Input, hitTest, forceRefresh, scrollbar and PWD paths are unchanged. The diff adds no user-facing strings, tenant-config writes, private data, or submodule changes. Project membership includes the production helper and behavioral tests in the appropriate targets.

Inspected the owner's retrieved Atlas result.json and build.log for invocation 41870fcc41c840d785ab666833d9ecf5: exact reviewed head, dirty=false, no overlay, compilation successful, actual XCTest execution with 11 tests and zero failures, and TEST SUCCEEDED. The tests exercise admission outcomes, stateful bursts, independent terminals, clearing, glyph preservation and a forty-stream replay. That replay establishes filter behavior, not measured live sidebar performance. No builds, tests, or app launches were performed by this reviewer. The review checkout was clean and diff --check passed.

The original ticket's window-title wording is superseded by the explicit plan clarification: WorkspaceManager retains the workspace-title policy. This PR prevents spinner-driven assignments; it does not make NSWindow.title follow OSC text.

## Runtime proof still required

The authorized low-risk ruling defers product proof to the merged-main Atlas Validator batch, so its present absence is not a blocker to this static review. Before product sign-off, that batch must show:

1. A tagged app suppresses standalone and unchanged-label spinner frames at the visible tab and metadata/observer paths, while successive real titles, the pre-flush return burst, clears and a second terminal behave as specified.
2. The window title retains the established workspace-title behavior without spinner-induced churn.
3. The same short replay on the pre-change base and merged build, with identical topology, records timings and load averages and demonstrates reduced title churn without input responsiveness regression. Pure admission counts are not this evidence.

Before landing, the Captain must gate on green required CI at the exact reviewed head. CI completion was not independently certified in this review. The batch must record its actual integrated SHA and preserve screenshots/metadata and timing evidence as specified in the validation comment.
